data.narrative:
Lilac Solutions, a Series C-stage Climate & Energy company founded by David Snydacker, has raised $315M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer set of 3 private companies at identical stage and sector (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amory) alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA), representing the frontier cleantech universe.

Stage-progression methodology applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a $536M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the 3-company same-stage, same-sector cohort yields $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy floor) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals ceiling). The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within the sector.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $455M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $768M. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to deployed capital; the peer-median approach introduces sector-specific risk and stage-risk premia evident in comparable recent raises. Key uncertainties include technology validation progress relative to peers, path to commercialization, and capital efficiency relative to the $700M–$3.0B peer bandwidth. The median estimate of $768M sits meaningfully below peer median, suggesting either a valuation discount to peer cohort or a more capital-efficient trajectory warranting closer diligence.
